gh_project_scope:
GitHub Board setup needs the write-capable `project` scope. Host: {host}. Active gh account: {active}. Safe scope status: {scopeStatus}. Project owner: {owner}{project}. Result: {summary}. Run:
`gh auth refresh -h github.com -s project`
then
`gh auth status --hostname github.com`
The refresh uses GitHub's browser/device flow. No token is requested. No mutation started.

For 403, ask a Project owner/admin to grant this account write access and confirm organization policies permit Projects. For 404, verify the derived owner, Project number, visibility, and that the account can see the owner's private Project. Check with `gh project list --owner {owner} --limit 100 --format json`. Check host/VPN/DNS for network failures. No mutation started.

A 403 requires Project write rights and compatible organization policy; a 404 means the Project or owner is not visible to this account. Confirm with `gh project view {number} --owner {owner}`. Ask a Project owner/admin to grant access. No mutation started.

github_project_manual_instructions:
Create the Project manually:
1. Sign in to the active GitHub account `{active}`. In GitHub, open “New project” and create it under owner `{owner}` (a User or Organization owner), using title `{title}`. Alternatively, use the verified GitHub CLI syntax: `gh project create --owner {owner} --title {title}`.
2. Confirm the Project actually exists under `{owner}` and grant the active account `{active}` write access; otherwise grant it under Project settings/members.
3. Confirm visibility and its number with: `gh project list --owner {owner} --limit 100 --format json`.
4. Rerun the copied Companion with `--project-number <number>`, or select the Project in the next TTY arrow-key menu.
`--dry-run` can never create a Project. For ongoing Project-v2 automation, `HEROES_PROJECT_TOKEN` needs only the `project` scope; repository operations continue to use `github.token`.

No local Companion state was written, and no automatic rollback is claimed. First check `gh project list --owner {owner} --limit 100 --format json` and do not create blindly again. No secret values were included in this message.

Run `squad upgrade --self` as your normal user; if a root-owned global npm install fails with EACCES or EPERM, repair it with `sudo sh -c 'umask 022 && exec npm install -g --allow-scripts=@bradygaster/squad-cli,node-pty,koffi,protobufjs @bradygaster/squad-cli@latest'`, not by running Squad itself under sudo. Restart the terminal, run `command -v squad`, `ls -l "$(command -v squad)"`, and `squad --version`, then run `squad upgrade` in the target repository and verify its marker before retrying.
help_text:
Usage:
  node .squad/templates/squad-heroes/companion/scripts/install --target /path/to/repository --repository owner/name --project-type 001 --deployment-branches 1 --deployment-branch-1 main [--model-reqeng ID] [--model-work ID] [--model-review ID] [--language de|en] [--dry-run] [--plan-json FILE | --json-plan]

Language: --language de|en > existing .squad/heroes.json > system locale (LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LANG, LANGUAGE). If no supported source is available, the installer fails and asks for --language de or --language en.

The Companion plans active scripts, prompts, workflows, and agent targets. The Squad plugin plan under templates/squad-heroes/companion/ is separate. TTY selection uses arrows or j/k, Enter, and Escape/q. CI supplies all model, branch, and Project flags. Conflicts are resolved locally, concisely, with a recommended merge. Use --decisions FILE for noninteractive decisions. Tokens are not accepted or printed.
